title: Thiriet by TDS wins rain-hit Imola
dek: Beche, Hirakawa and Thiriet won the 4 Hours of Imola in the #46 Oreca from second on the grid, as a downpour in the final hour left G-Drive second and DragonSpeed third.

chapters.title: G-Drive arrives as the leader
text: The second round of the 2016 European Le Mans Series took the paddock to Imola on 15 May, with LMP2 in an unusual shape. G-Drive Racing arrived as championship leader after winning at Silverstone, with the SMP Racing BR01 #32 second there and the Lombard-run Ligier #22 a surprise third. Thiriet by TDS Racing and Eurasia Motorsport, both billed as title rivals, had both gone home from the opener without a classified finish, and the Imola race was the chance to put points on the board. The class had shrunk to 14 cars: the second SMP entry was absent and the Garage 56 Morgan was saved for the Le Mans test days. Imola was also a four-hour race with an eye on the 24 Hours of Le Mans a month later, and several line-ups reflected that.

Krohn Racing's #40 Ligier lost Tracy Krohn, who was barred from sporting activity until 25 May after an injury suffered in training at home. Bjorn Wirdheim, the 2015 ELMS champion, stood in alongside Niclas Jonsson and Olivier Pla, who was back after missing Silverstone for Ford GTE duty. Murphy Prototypes reshuffled the #48 Oreca 03R with Sean Doyle, Garry Findlay and Patrick McClughan, while Race Performance's #34 Oreca welcomed Shinji Nakano in place of Franck Mailleux. Practice belonged to Panis Barthez Competition: Paul Loup Chatin topped both sessions in the #23 Ligier, with a 1:34.435 on Friday and a 1:33.881 on Saturday morning. FP2 was a messy affair of full-course yellows and a red flag, and it ended the weekend of SMP's #32, which Stefano Coletti sent into the tyres at Variante Villeneuve, ripping the steering wheel from its column.

chapters.title: Four cars within 44 thousandths
text: Qualifying produced one of the tightest LMP2 sessions of the season. Nicolas Lapierre put the DragonSpeed Oreca #21 on pole with a 1:33.780 on his final lap, and the top four were covered by 0.044 seconds. Mathias Beche took the Thiriet by TDS Oreca #46 to second with a 1:33.815 despite having to go off the road to avoid a spinning Race Performance car on his last attempt. Chatin set exactly the same time in the Panis Barthez Ligier #23 but was placed third because he had set it later in the session; the team had topped both practice sessions and left without a pole to show for it. Olivier Pla was fourth for Krohn Racing, ahead of Giedo van der Garde in the G-Drive Gibson #38, with Gommendy's Eurasia Oreca sixth and the Greaves Ligier seventh.

SMP's #32 BR01 made it to the grid only after lengthy repairs, with bodywork borrowed from the team's second car from Silverstone, and started twelfth. Lapierre's pole carried a bonus championship point. In all, 41 cars were due to start, after Formula Racing's GTE Ferrari was withdrawn following a heavy crash in FP2.

chapters.title: Lapierre leads, then loses out in the pits
text: The race started under blue skies, with Lapierre leading the field into the first corner and Pierre Thiriet's #46 Oreca keeping pace until Chatin passed it. Early on Greaves Motorsport's #41 Ligier was clipped by the Murphy Oreca and spun at Curva Tosa, rejoined last and was effectively out of the running; the Murphy driver was shown a black and white flag. Lapierre built a lead of about four seconds before he met the GTE traffic, where a Ferrari moved across on him and forced him onto the grass. He kept the car straight, set the fastest lap of the race, and handed over to Henrik Hedman at the first stops.

The pit stops reshuffled the order. Thiriet and Chatin both stayed in their cars, and their quicker stops took them past the DragonSpeed entry. Chatin led the #23 Ligier, but Thiriet sat three to four seconds behind him in the #46.

chapters.title: Hirakawa takes the lead, G-Drive climbs
text: After the second stops, Thiriet handed over to Ryo Hirakawa and Chatin to Fabien Barthez. Hirakawa caught Fabien Barthez and moved into the lead on lap 59 around the inside at Rivazza, then pulled out a gap of about ten seconds. Just before the halfway mark the first full-course yellow was called when a Graff LMP3 Ligier went into the gravel; it lasted five minutes. About 20 minutes later a second was needed to recover another LMP3 car stopped at the final corner. Panis Barthez faded from the fight and eventually finished seventh.

The most dramatic recovery came from G-Drive. Silver-rated Simon Dolan started the Gibson #38, and Harry Tincknell took over in sixth place before moving rapidly forward. By the time van der Garde took over with 80 minutes to run, the car was second, ahead of Hanley in the DragonSpeed Oreca. Beche took over from Hirakawa for the final 90 minutes with a comfortable cushion, and SMP's #32 and the Eurasia Oreca #33, steady for Gommendy and Pu Junjin, ran fourth and fifth.

chapters.title: Rain ends the race under the safety car
text: With 70 minutes left, dark clouds gathered over Imola and the rain was soon torrential. A full-course yellow was called as cars spun, the leader among them, though Beche recovered without losing his advantage. When the yellow stayed out, with several drivers struggling to keep up under it, the race director replaced it with the safety car with 27 minutes remaining. The track did not dry, and the race ran its full four hours before ending behind the safety car, with no overtaking allowed on the final lap.

Beche therefore crossed the line first for Thiriet by TDS, with Pierre Thiriet and Hirakawa, 121 laps completed. G-Drive's #38 finished 19.257 seconds back in second, while DragonSpeed's #21 took third, 30.810 seconds behind, a podium the team was thrilled with. SMP's #32 finished fourth ahead of Eurasia's #33. Krohn's Ligier and the Panis Barthez Ligier were sixth and seventh, a lap down, the latter having slipped back after offs in the downpour. Algarve Pro Racing's #25 and IDEC Sport's #28 finished the day not classified.

chapters.title: A first win for Thiriet by TDS
text: Beche said it had been a great race after the bad luck at Silverstone, regretting only that it ended under the safety car for the public, and added that the team now hoped for a good result at Le Mans. The victory, the first of 2016 for Thiriet by TDS, was worth 25 points after the opening-round retirement. DragonSpeed's third place was the team's best result of the season so far, and with the bonus point for pole, Lapierre, Hedman and Hanley left with 16 points. Panis Barthez Competition, quickest in both practice sessions and a contender for the lead in the first half, finished seventh, a lap down on the winners at the end of the day.

The championship picture tightened at the top. G-Drive collected 18 points for second and extended its LMP2 lead to 13 points over the SMP Racing #32, which finished fourth after its FP2 crash and a rebuilt car. The Silverstone winners had now scored on both race days, while the teams that retired at the opener, Thiriet by TDS and Eurasia, had begun to repair their seasons. Eurasia took fifth after a quiet, solid run for Gommendy and Pu Junjin.

Race control's decision was the main talking point. Race director Eduardo Freitas had only three options once the rain returned: the red flag, an immediate safety car or a full-course yellow, and he chose the last before moving to the safety car. Some argued the field could have restarted for the final 25 minutes, but the concern was releasing cars in marginal conditions after a day of near-constant off-track excursions. Greaves Motorsport's Rojas, spun early by the Murphy Oreca, finished eighth, three laps down, ahead of the Race Performance and Murphy entries.
Several teams and drivers now turned to the Le Mans 24 Hours. The championship resumes with the 4 Hours of Red Bull Ring on 17 July.

facts.v: The top four in qualifying were within 0.044 seconds, and Lapierre's 1:33.780 gave DragonSpeed pole.
